clue.text: Witness signature and stay low

blocks.note: read with what follows: to stay put is not to do something
to stay low is not to get up, and getting up is to arise

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to sign as a witness and keep their head down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay low' is read as a whole: if you stay low you do NOT ARISE, and those two words run together to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary formally certifies documents, so to notarise is to attest officially that a signature is genuine.

clue.text: Drink is handy when holding court

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: handy means close by, within reach
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A drink is close at hand while someone is in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' is the adjective for close by, not skilful, which is what makes the container work.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods, and the word is used generally for any delicious beverage or fruit juice.

clue.text: Warm and comfortable where little piggy went?

blocks.note: first meaning: snug and cosy
second meaning, read as three words: the destination of a pig going home

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme pig ends up somewhere cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: A pig lives in a sty, so a little pig heading home went TO A STY, which runs together as the answer; the question mark flags the liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal adjective for pleasantly heated and snug, like bread just out of the toaster.

clue.text: 13 or 15 creative art – ‘e by gum!

indicators.note: being creative means making something new, so the letters are remade in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, the dropped-h 'e and all

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in northern English dialect at a piece of creative art.
explanation.walkthrough: '13 or 15' looks like a cross-reference to other clues, but it is the definition. 'By gum' is a mild northern English oath, and 'e is a dropped-h 'he'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby league side fields thirteen players and a rugby union side fifteen, so the numbers each describe one squad.

clue.text: Here in California Arab tans easily and another heads north

indicators.note: done easily means done loosely and freely, so the letters fall into a relaxed new order
in a down entry, going north means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
another of the same, a second Arab

explanation.surface: In California an Arab tans easily while a companion sets off northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second copy of the word Arab just used, which is then flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Barbara is a coastal city in Southern California, so 'here in California' points to one place in that state.

clue.text: Rightwing extremist leaders are unable to back down

indicators.note: leaders are the ones out in front, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
are unable to means can't, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Far-right party leaders cannot bring themselves to climb down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like a noun for the extremists' bosses, but it only picks out letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement or belief formally, which is to retreat from a position one previously held.

clue.text: Praise would be accurate if penultimately doubled

blocks.clueFragment: would be accurate if penultimately doubled
blocks.note: surface reading: a compliment becomes true if something near the end is said twice

blocks.clueFragment: would be accurate if penultimately doubled
blocks.note: setter's reading: the second-last letter is a Roman numeral, and twice its value is another numeral, which turns the word into one meaning precise

explanation.surface: Flattery would be truthful if repeated near the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The second-last letter of EXALT is L, Roman 50; doubled it becomes 100, which is C, and EXALT becomes EXACT, meaning accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to glorify or extol them highly, the same as lavishing acclaim upon them.

clue.text: Divine food as originally barbecued with Maori cooking

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the following word is kept
cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food fit for the gods, cooked as a Maori barbecue would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' adds the Maori letters to the others before the whole lot is mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ambrosia was the food of the gods that granted immortality, hence heavenly fare.

clue.text: You old smooth number

blocks.note: thou is the archaic form of you
to sand wood is to smooth it

explanation.surface: Someone addresses an old smoothie of a song or dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song or a person, but it is the definition; 'You old' is a pointer to an old-fashioned form of the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is a specific numerical value, ten hundreds, so it is one example of a figure.

clue.text: Adjustment of direction that may lead to source

blocks.note: first meaning: a switch of heading, as by a ship or a plan
second meaning, read cryptically: an operation on a six-letter word that rearranges it into another

explanation.surface: A river's altered route might take an explorer back to its spring.
explanation.walkthrough: COURSE with its letters changed becomes SOURCE, so changing COURSE literally leads to SOURCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing course means steering a ship or plan onto a different heading, an alteration of route.

clue.text: Perennial barking first thing in the morning and we don’t like it

indicators.note: the first thing of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
AM is the abbreviation for before noon
what a crowd shouts in disapproval

explanation.surface: A dog barking at dawn, and nobody enjoys it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First thing in the morning' reads as one phrase but splits: 'first thing' acts on 'barking', and 'in the morning' is AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a woody grass that lives for many years, and perennial as a noun means a plant that does so.

clue.text: Bombshell at heart interested in flying BA or SAS for example

indicators.note: the heart of something is its middle, so a piece is placed in the centre of another
simply placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: BB is Brigitte Bardot, the French film star famed as a blonde bombshell
RE means concerning or in the matter of, which is what one is interested in
aviation is the business of flying aircraft

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman is keen on travelling with an airline such as BA or SAS.
explanation.walkthrough: BA and SAS look like airlines in a flying surface, but they are offered as examples of shortened names. Brigitte Bardot was known by her initials, and both short pieces go in together.
explanation.definitionFit: BA (British Airways) and SAS (Scandinavian Airlines) are initial-letter shortenings, which are instances of shortened written forms.

clue.text: Tory leader in foul play as might be expected

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is used
placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
something foul breaks the rules, so these letters are put out of their proper order

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Conservative party chief caught in foul play, which surprises nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul play' reads as a set phrase, but 'foul' only works on 'play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptly means fittingly or appropriately, in a way that suits the situation, much as one would predict.

clue.text: Victim of mariner as Borstal delinquent

indicators.note: a delinquent goes astray, so these letters wander out of line

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor's victim is likened to a young offender in detention.
explanation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British reform school for young offenders, which fits 'delinquent' on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, the sailor shoots this seabird and is cursed for killing it.

clue.text: Returning pointer running wild around chambers

indicators.note: something running wild is out of control, so the letters break out of their order
going around something encloses it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
the atria are the upper chambers of the heart

explanation.surface: A gun dog dashes about some rooms on its way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' is a breed of gun dog on the surface; 'chambers' means the chambers of the heart, not rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Repatriation is the act of sending or coming back to one's own country, a homecoming.

clue.text: Tech industry quickly conceals mounting affliction

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
to conceal something is to keep it inside, so one piece hides within another

blocks.note: a sore is a painful spot, an ailment
apace means swiftly

explanation.surface: The technology sector rushes to hide a growing malaise.
explanation.walkthrough: APACE opens after its first letter to take the flipped piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerospace covers the high-technology business of building aircraft and spacecraft, a major engineering sector.

clue.text: Definitive hospital having slipped becoming compassionate

indicators.note: a thing that has slipped is no longer in its proper place, so the order changes

blocks.note: definitive and emphatic both mean forceful and conclusive
H is the abbreviation for hospital; this is the letter that moves

explanation.surface: A firm hospital, after an accident, turns into a caring one.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the H moves: in EMPHATIC it slips two places down to sit after the T, and the word becomes EMPATHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being empathic means sharing and understanding another person's feelings, which is what sympathetic kindness involves.

clue.text: New edition about a thoughtful process

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are rebuilt in another order
being about something means surrounding it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new edition of a book concerns some careful method of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New edition' reads as a publishing phrase, but 'New' only works on the letters of 'edition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideation is the forming of ideas or concepts, a mental activity carried out by thinking.

clue.text: Novel crossbeam rigged by egg-producer

indicators.note: a rigged result is fixed by tampering, so these letters are interfered with
standing by something means next to it, so the parts sit side by side

blocks.note: cross and mad both mean angry
taken as written
one printed word that the wordplay splits into two pieces
the ovary is the organ that produces egg cells

explanation.surface: A rigged-up crossbeam beside a hen house, painted as fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossbeam' must be split: 'cross' is a word for angry and only 'beam' is mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Bovary is Gustave Flaubert's 1857 French book about Emma Bovary's adultery, a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: See 9 Across
Managed to interrupt shock therapy, rising in a semiconscious state

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside another
in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A patient comes round from electric shock treatment in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: The therapy letters flip first, then RAN breaks in after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dazed, half-aware condition like hypnosis, where the person is neither fully awake nor asleep.

clue.text: Puzzler’s song about gold limo?

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round the rest

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a limo is a kind of car

explanation.surface: A setter's tune about a golden limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was the pen name of John Graham, the much-loved Guardian setter; the araucaria is also the monkey puzzle tree, hence a double sense of 'Puzzler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria was a celebrated compiler of Guardian crosswords, so he was a maker of puzzles, and the name is a tree called monkey puzzle.

clue.text: Bum and dunderhead locked up?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, so only the opening letter is used
something locked up is shut inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: the opening letter of this part of the word
one printed word that splits into a source and a selector
where something is locked up: a cage

explanation.surface: A layabout and an idiot both end up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locked up' does double duty: it says one piece is enclosed and names the enclosure, a CAGE. 'Bum' is the verb, as in to bum a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is slang for begging or scrounging it, which is exactly what cadging means.

clue.text: After saucy crosswords to begin with, the Guardian’s getting clean

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is the opening, so only first letters are kept
coming after places one part behind another in sequence

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
the newspaper speaking of itself says 'our'

explanation.surface: The Guardian cleans up its act after a run of risqué puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: This puzzle appeared in the Guardian, so 'the Guardian's' is what the paper calls its own: OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub hard with something abrasive, a vigorous way of washing a surface.

clue.text: Bob possibly first to hear radio broadcast

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening, so only that letter is used
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob might be the first to catch a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but it is the haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short hairstyle cut level around the head, one example of a styled cut.

clue.text: Entertainment coverage for home sides taking a last dash

indicators.note: taking something on means adding it, so the parts join in sequence
coverage wraps over something, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: fun is amusement or entertainment
at home means in
taken as written
the two sides are left and right, L and R

explanation.surface: A TV channel covers the home teams making a late sprint for victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home sides' looks like home teams in a match, but 'home' and 'sides' are separate pieces, and the sides are the two of a road or stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A final run is the closing sprint or attempt, so it describes the last burst of speed.

clue.text: Ride through African territory

indicators.note: something that runs through spans the words, so the letters straddle the gap

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A horseback journey across part of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' looks like a preposition of travel, but it signals letters running across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A canter is a gentle gait of a horse, and to canter is to go on horseback at that pace.

clue.text: Tennis player heard chasing bet to come first

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so a word is chosen for its sound not its spelling
one that chases runs behind, so this part goes after the other

blocks.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
a top-ranked tennis player in a draw is a seed

explanation.surface: A tennis star chases a wager in order to finish top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tennis player' wants a name, but tennis players ranked in a draw are seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede is to precede in time or order, so it means going before something else.
